thread:
ops-bot: INCIDENT OPENED — sev2. Detected widespread 5xxs for tenant 'Cedar' (enterprise, VPC/dedicated) in eu-west. Source: frontend-nginx cluster eu-west-1. Initial alert: spike in 503 + p95 token latency. Paging oncall.

julie_oncall: ack — I'm on it. paging @tom_neteng @maya_prodeng @eric_sre @amanda_csm. can someone pull quick customer impact? :rotating_light:

eric_sre: looking at app logs now. rapid increase in `upstream timed out (110)` coming from the dedicated pool routers to model workers. Lots of `grpc: deadline exceeded`. stacktrace excerpt:
```
2026-03-15T18:02:11Z frontend-1 nginx[pid]: 503 upstream timed out while reading response
2026-03-15T18:02:13Z router-3 model-proxy[pid]: rpc error: code = DeadlineExceeded desc = context deadline exceeded
```
p50 latency fine, p95 > 2s and error rate ~12% for Cedar eu-west. likely capacity or routing mismatch to warm pool.

tom_neteng: checking DNS and load balancing. Cedar is on dedicated pool `cedar-eu-west-primary` with warm standby `cedar-eu-west-warm`. Route53 record `cedar.api.example.redwood` has ALIAS to LB primary. TTL currently 60s (we lowered earlier this morning). I can start failover via DNS + LB reweighting. Recommend: do a staged traffic shift to warm pool (20% -> 60% -> 100%) and monitor.

maya_prodeng: agree. We'll also need to warm KV caches on the warm pool and increase replicas. Starting warm pool scale now:
```
# quick warm
redwoodctl scale --pool cedar-eu-west-warm --replicas 4
redwoodctl warm-cache --tenant cedar --pool cedar-eu-west-warm --prefixes default
```
Expect ~60s for new replicas to report healthy.

devon_platform: prepare traffic-shift job. We'll use platform routing to steer percentages (preferred over immediate DNS cutover). Command:
```
routingctl shift --tenant cedar --region eu-west --from cedar-eu-west-primary --to cedar-eu-west-warm --percent 20
```
I'll kick off 20% canary now.

deploy-bot: canary start event: routing shift 20% -> cedar-eu-west-warm by devon_platform at 18:08 UTC.

julie_oncall: monitoring metrics: request success rate for Cedar at 20% shift: errors drop to 6% on primary, warm pool reporting 1.2% error but higher latency on first few requests (cache cold). Keep the canary for 10m.

amanda_csm: I reached Cedar ops (Eve). Told them we're doing staged failover and asked them to pause large batch jobs. They acknowledged and will watch dashboards. Customer impact note: interactive API calls degraded ~8% for last 20m; some jobs may have retried.

eric_sre: log patterns show backlog clearing on primary as shift continues. I'm seeing some KV cache misses on warm pool causing slow tails. Suggest we pre-warm specific tenant prefixes (we started that).

tom_neteng: starting second step: reweight to 60% to warm pool.

deploy-bot: routing update: 60% -> cedar-eu-west-warm by devon_platform at 18:22 UTC.

julie_oncall: after 60% shift error rate overall down to 1.5%, p95 latency stable ~800ms. No new 503 alerts. Good.

devon_platform: preparing final cutover. Two options: full routing switch via control-plane reweight OR DNS cutover (TTL is low so DNS is viable if we want to avoid control-plane churn). Given we control routing, prefer reweight to 100% now.

tom_neteng: one caveat: some VPC peering routes for Cedar tied to primary LB. I'll verify that no private-network path breaks. Running `ip route` checks and LB health checks now.

eric_sre: confirming model worker pools are healthy on warm: all readiness probes passing.

alex_oncall: I'm taking handoff for the next 2h to keep watch during final cut. julie handing over now. :handshake:

julie_oncall: handing to @alex_oncall — all current actions in progress: warm scaled, caches warming, 60% traffic on warm. I'll stay available for 30m.

alex_oncall: ack. I'll run the final 100% shift in ~5m if metrics look stable.

deploy-bot: preflight check OK: no critical alerts, LB target counts healthy.

devon_platform: executing final shift to 100%.

deploy-bot: routing update: 100% -> cedar-eu-west-warm by devon_platform at 18:40 UTC.

julie_oncall: monitoring: error rate back to baseline (0.3%), latency healthy. Cedar ops confirm customer reports normal behavior.

amanda_csm: Cedar support: "Thanks — traffic looks normal now. We'll let you know if anything pops up."

eric_sre: initial hypothesis: primary pool experienced transient overload/backpressure — possibly degraded kernel threads on a subset of model workers causing RPC timeouts. We'll collect traces and coredumps for postmortem. Ticketing note: attach logs from `router-3` and `model-proxy`.

tom_neteng: no DNS cutover required; routing shift succeeded. We'll revert any temporary ACL or routing changes after stabilization. TTL remains 60 until we mark incident resolved.

alex_oncall: closing actions: continue 30m watch, keep warm pool at scaled replica count for 1h, schedule escalation to infra-reliability if errors reappear. I'll create the follow-up JIRA and link to this thread.

julie_oncall: thanks all. Postmortem owners: eric_sre (root cause), tom_neteng (routing/DNS), devon_platform (runbook updates), amanda_csm (customer comms). I'll start the postmortem doc template: https://redwood.internal/pm/cedar-eu-west-failover

ops-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigated — traffic successfully shifted to warm pool; monitoring in watch window. Severity downgraded to sev3.

alex_oncall: incident resolved for now. final note: runbook gap: add explicit steps to pre-warm caches for enterprise warm pools and automated reweight threshold to trigger earlier. Filing follow-ups.

julie_oncall: closing incident in 30m if no regressions. great coordination everyone. :tada:
